sentences.text: Researchers examined whether biological sex, puberty timing, and childhood mental health symptoms could predict changes in visual attention brain waves from childhood to adulthood using a longitudinal cohort design with 531 youth who performed a reaction-time task at five specific ages between 2010 and 2025.

The study found that the visual P300 brain wave, a specific neural marker of attention, showed a curved decline pattern from late childhood into early adulthood, with boys exhibiting higher levels of externalizing behaviors or depression symptoms at age 9 starting with lower baseline visual P300 brain waves.
The authors conclude that further research is needed to understand how these neural attention markers develop and connect to future mental health issues.
